sec: Biochemical screening, imaging and surgical TOC · p856

items.q: The SCREENING test for pheochromocytoma (98% sensitivity and specificity) is:
items.exp: 24 hr fractionated metanephrine/NM is the screening test with 98% sensitivity and 98% specificity. (Book p856)

items.q: Plasma fractionated metanephrine/NM has what sensitivity (no false negatives)?
items.exp: Plasma fractionated metanephrine/NM: 100% sensitivity; done along with 24 hr urine if very strong family history. (Book p856)

items.q: The IOC for adrenal pheochromocytoma on imaging is:
items.exp: MRI abdomen is IOC, showing T2 hyperintensities with hemorrhagic/cystic changes. (Book p856)

items.q: Which two imaging modalities are now obsolete?
items.exp: MIBG and FDG-PET are obsolete now. (Book p856)

items.q: Gallium DOTATATE PET scan is the IOC when:
opts: MRI is negative but biochemical tests are positive (paraganglioma)
items.exp: Ga-DOTATATE PET is IOC if MRI negative but biochemically positive (paraganglioma). (Book p856)

items.q: The DOTATATE principle is: DOTA–octreotate binds to:
opts: Somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2) on the tumour surface
items.exp: DOTA → octreotate binds somatostatin receptor type 2 on the tumour surface. (Book p856)

items.q: The treatment of choice for pheochromocytoma is:
items.exp: Laparoscopic retroperitoneal adrenalectomy is TOC. (Book p856)

items.q: Pre-surgical preparation begins how many days before surgery (admit + liberal fluids)?
items.exp: 10 days before surgery: admit patient and give liberal fluid intake (then BP control). (Book p856)
